properties.description:
`Interface.designation` carries the boundary's external ROLE — `published` (offers), `required` (needs one from outside), `both`, or `internal` — and `pair_designs` matches COMPLEMENTS across two designs: published/both against required/both, never like with like. The `required` half did not exist before 2026-07-30, which is why a design could say what it offered but not what it needed in any form another design could be matched against.

Two boundaries pair when their names match fuzzily (reusing ingest's two-band resolution rather than a second matcher) AND they agree on `medium`, `transport_security` and `auth`. Five outcomes: paired, CONFLICTS (names match, axes refuse — reported with every refusing axis), unmet needs, dead surface, and duplicate providers. Uncertain names are candidates to ask about, never actions. Boundaries with no role are counted and named, because `internal` is the default and cannot distinguish a deliberate choice from an unlabelled one. Produces the pairs `seam_report` previously had to be handed by a person.
properties.name: Two designs pair by complementary role, so the seam is computed rather than hand-wired
